description: Which ontology rules the running application actually enforces. 'runtime' means a contract test executes the real code path and it rejects the bad case, within the stated scope. 'offline_only' means only tools/validate_ontology.py checks it, against fixtures; no live workflow calls the validator. 'planned' means the application does not do this today. A contract can pass and still leave its shape 'offline_only' when no deployed caller of that code is established.

sources.reason: A relationship row cannot hold 'deprecated'; only an entity row can. A superseded relationship row is stored as 'rejected' and its proposal as 'deprecated' (ADR-0017 amended, #5523).
Tag rows have no deprecated state.
Wiring rows have no deprecated state.

sources.name: KG_APPROVAL_STATES
sources.reason: The engine-side writer never emits 'deprecated'; supersede writes 'rejected' on the row (ADR-0017 amended, #5523).
The live-snapshot decoder uses three bands of its own; it never reports 'bad' or 'uncertain' and calls an undecodable tag 'unknown'. No tracking issue yet; listed as a remaining gap in #5528.

stale-drive-data-gives-no-diagnosis.rule: A reading taken while drive comms are lost is not used for a live diagnosis or a numeric claim.
stale-drive-data-gives-no-diagnosis.call_path: mira-bots/shared/engine.py -> live_snapshot.normalize + render_machine_evidence -> build_drive_diagnostic; mira-pipeline/ignition_chat.py -> live_snapshot.assess_from_paths -> build_drive_diagnostic; mira-bots/ask_api/app.py -> normalize + render_status_block

fault-code-answer-is-scoped-to-one-drive.rule: A fault code is answered only from the one drive family the question resolved to; two families in one question is refused.
fault-code-answer-is-scoped-to-one-drive.call_path: mira-bots/ask_api/drive_pack.py and mira-bots/shared/engine.py -> drive_packs.ask.answer_question; mira-bots/shared/chat/fast_paths.py -> resolve_service_pack

command-is-not-feedback.rule: A RUN command is never taken as proof the motor is running; the two are separate tags and a mismatch is reported.
command-is-not-feedback.call_path: The gateway endpoint ignition/webdev/FactoryLM/api/diagnose/doGet.py calls a vendored copy, diagnose_core.evaluate (the test runs both the source and the copy). No DEPLOYED caller is established: the WebDev module is not installed on the bench gateway, so that endpoint does not answer today.

approval-state-vocabulary-is-a-database-.rule: A graph row cannot carry an approval state outside the allowed set.
approval-state-vocabulary-is-a-database-.call_path: PostgreSQL CHECK constraint on kg_entities / kg_relationships (every writer)

asset-agent-approval-needs-a-named-perso.rule: An asset agent cannot be approved without a named human actor.
asset-agent-approval-needs-a-named-perso.call_path: simlab/approval.py -> validate_transition; mira-pipeline/ignition_chat.py -> gate_decision. The Hub route api/assets/[id]/agent-status/transition uses the TypeScript twin, which this test does not execute; the same rule is asserted there by mira-hub/src/lib/asset-agent-transition.test.ts ('approved requires a human actor'), run by the Hub Unit Tests CI job.

superseded-fact-leaves-the-verified-set.rule: A superseded assertion must not remain verified (R14c).
superseded-fact-leaves-the-verified-set.call_path: ADR-0017 as amended 2026-11-14 (#5523): the supersede transition moves the relationship row from 'verified' to 'rejected' (a relationship row cannot hold 'deprecated'; the proposal's 'deprecated' status records why). Python: apply_kg_approval(trigger='supersede') writes 'rejected' — executed by the test named here on a real PostgreSQL. Hub: applyHubProposalTransition('supersede') demotes the edge in the same transaction — executed by mira-hub/tests/integration/ontology/bench-context-contract.integration.test.ts (propose -> /api/proposals/[id]/decide -> traversal -> supersede), which runs in NO CI job. LIMITS: no route or scheduled job fires 'supersede' for a graph edge today, so this is a correct transition with no production caller; the only importer of the Python helper outside tests is demo/factory_difference_engine/pipeline.py; readers that apply no approval_state filter still list the retired row.

fault-code-identity-includes-the-model.rule: Two models' fault codes are different things even when the code text matches (model vs installed-instance identity, R4).
fault-code-identity-includes-the-model.call_path: mira-crawler ingest -> kg_writer.register_fault_code -> upsert_entity keyed (tenant, type, name)

reader-sees-the-relationship-name-approv.rule: An approved relationship must be visible to the reader that is meant to use it.
reader-sees-the-relationship-name-approv.call_path: Repaired for #5519 by one shared read view derived from the writer's own name mapping; traversal.ts, context-builder.ts, plan-vs-actual.ts and uns-backfill.ts read through it. The test named here is SOURCE-LEVEL ONLY (it reads the TypeScript files: the reader touches the bare table in exactly one place, the fault-OCCURRENCE count, and the view is built from the writer's mapping). The EXECUTED proof is mira-hub/tests/integration/ontology/bench-context-contract.integration.test.ts on a real PostgreSQL (approved feeds / has_component / similar_to / parent_of / caused_by edges are read in the right direction, once) — it runs in NO CI job. LIMITS: two legacy names share one stored name (located_at and parent_of -> LOCATED_IN; had_fault and exhibited_fault -> HAS_FAILURE_MODE), so a reader cannot tell which was meant; the external read API exposes stored names.

live-summary-does-not-take-a-command-as-.rule: The drive summary a technician reads must not say the machine is running on the strength of a RUN command alone, and must not hide a RUN command against STOPPED feedback.
live-summary-does-not-take-a-command-as-.call_path: DEPLOYED: mira-pipeline/ignition_chat.py -> live_snapshot.assess_from_paths -> normalize -> build_drive_diagnostic -> assess_snapshots; the contract test calls assess_from_paths. Also wired but with no in-repo caller passing live_tags: mira-bots/shared/engine.py -> normalize -> render_machine_evidence. mira-bots/ask_api/app.py uses normalize + render_status_block only and does not produce this summary. The equipment-notebook chat does NOT use this module (see mira-hub/tests/integration/ontology/bench-pilot-live-evidence.integration.test.ts; TypeScript, local only, no CI job).

missing-fault-reading-is-not-reported-he.rule: A fault register that was never read must not be summarised as 'no active fault'.
missing-fault-reading-is-not-reported-he.call_path: DEPLOYED: mira-pipeline/ignition_chat.py -> live_snapshot.assess_from_paths -> normalize -> build_drive_diagnostic -> assess_snapshots; the contract test calls assess_from_paths. Also wired but with no in-repo caller passing live_tags: mira-bots/shared/engine.py -> normalize -> render_machine_evidence. mira-bots/ask_api/app.py uses normalize + render_status_block only and does not produce this summary. The equipment-notebook chat does NOT use this module (see mira-hub/tests/integration/ontology/bench-pilot-live-evidence.integration.test.ts; TypeScript, local only, no CI job).

drive-reading-age-affects-quality.rule: A drive reading's quality must reflect its age.
drive-reading-age-affects-quality.call_path: live_snapshot.normalize, called directly by the test. Callers: mira-bots/ask_api/app.py and mira-bots/shared/engine.py pass the receive time (datetime.now) as the stamp; mira-pipeline/ignition_chat.py -> assess_from_paths passes an empty stamp. No caller passes the reading's own time, and nothing compares a stamp with the present.

BooleanNotQuantityShape.nearest_runtime: tag_events.value_type CHECK fixes the type vocabulary only

ClockProvenanceShape.nearest_runtime: tag_events keeps both event and ingest clocks and the notebook replay renders both; the GS10 live-snapshot path stamps one caller-supplied receive time on every reading

CommandNotFeedbackShape.nearest_runtime: CV-101 anomaly rule A6 keeps the run command and run feedback apart, but the gateway endpoint that would run it is not installed. The deployed GS10 summary (live_snapshot.assess_snapshots) does the opposite: a RUN command alone is reported as running. The notebook chat's own summary path does keep them apart (TypeScript test, local only).

LiveDiagnosisEligibilityShape.scope: GS10 live-snapshot path, when a turn carries live tags; only the comms-lost case. There is no age-based staleness check

MeasurementCompletenessShape.nearest_runtime: tag_events NOT NULL columns and quality CHECK

StaleCommsNumericClaimShape.scope: GS10 live-snapshot path, when a turn carries live tags

FaultAppliedToWrongFamilyShape.scope: Drive-pack answers only. The knowledge-graph path does not enforce it (#5520)

AssertionShape.scope: The approval_state vocabulary only, on kg_entities and kg_relationships (each table has its own allowed set). The shape's other constraints, such as confidence range, are offline only

InferenceCannotSelfApproveShape.nearest_runtime: asset_agent_transition requires a named actor for asset-agent approval (contract asset-agent-approval-needs-a-named-person); nothing equivalent guards a graph assertion
